title: Critical Logarithm in Minimax Wasserstein-One Risk for Counterfactual Laws on the Square

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching sqrt(log(en)/n) upper and lower expected W1 risks, a total finite probability estimator, and an actual-law all-procedure converse. Maximality widened the class to arbitrary controls, treated-only causal assumptions, and one-sided treatment positivity; all seven cited leaves were lawfully attested and the mathematics panel passed. Field novelty failed at a 7.1 ceiling against 7.4; the sound result is subfield. No Lean formalization was launched, and six non-tier-causing ballast wrappers remain.
tldr: The exact minimax expected Euclidean \(W_1\) risk for the marginal treated potential-outcome law on the two-dimensional square is \(\sqrt{\log(en)/n}\). Identification uses treated consistency \(A Y=A Y(1)\), treated exchangeability \(Y(1)\perp A\mid X\), and only one-sided treated positivity \(e(x)\in[1/4,1]\), allowing certain treatment. The causal class has unknown quarter-H\"older propensity and treated-density covariate sections, positive treated densities, and Lipschitz outcome sections. The untreated potential outcome is otherwise unrestricted, and observed controls may follow any measurable kernel on the square. A cubic marked correction with pilot clipping to \([1/4,1]\), Neumann-norm aggregation, and deterministic finite-grid probability projection give a total observable attainer. An actual-law supported multiscale prior gives the matching all-procedure converse. The nuisance elbow adds no logarithmic factor to the direct Lipschitz-density benchmark.
gap: The exact critical factor remains unmatched in the direct square-density comparison. Unknown quarter-smooth causal nuisances introduce a second equality case whose simultaneous coefficient control is absent from scalar theory.
fill: Derive the explicit sharp sequence, a total finite-data distribution estimator and a matching converse on the unchanged experiment; establish whether observational nuisance learning changes the direct benchmark.
